name: Lake Mereldar
summary: Lake Mereldar's waters south of Corin's Crossing have turned foul and corrupted. Once part of Lordaeron's rural heartland, the lake now breeds twisted elementals beneath the Scourge's lingering taint.

sections.title: A Polluted Haven
sections.body:
South of Corin's Crossing, Lake Mereldar rests among the old farms of northern Lordaeron. Ruins of a homestead, an abandoned shack, and a worn ferry mark its shores. Farmers and travelers once crossed its gentle waters by ferry.

Then the Scourge brought its plague of undeath, and the lake and its surroundings fell into ruin. The soil withered, and the water turned foul and poisonous.

sections.title: Twisted Inhabitants
sections.body:
The blight in Lake Mereldar has tainted the water and the spirits bound to it. Blighted Surges are corrupted water elementals, driven mad by necromantic residue. They lurk in the shallows and surface without warning.

Plague Ravagers prowl the muddy, weed-choked banks. They hunt living creatures that stray near the dead shoreline.

faq.answer: Lake Mereldar lies in the central-southern Eastern Plaguelands, directly south of Corin's Crossing.

faq.q: Why are there water elementals in the lake?
faq.answer: Blighted Surges are water elementals twisted into hostile creatures by necromantic blight that seeped into the lake during Lordaeron's fall.

faq.q: Who owned the shack and ferry on the shore?
faq.answer: The shack and ferry belonged to a local farming homestead established before the Third War. When the plague ravaged the Eastweald, the homesteaders perished or fled, leaving them to rot.

faq.q: Is the water safe to drink or swim in?
faq.answer: No. The plague of undeath fouls the lake, making its water dangerous to drink, swim in, or harvest from. Blighted creatures dwell there too.

angles.text: As a shaman, you can see how the Scourge's foul magic twists natural elemental spirits into mindless, violent horrors like the Blighted Surges of Lake Mereldar.
